## Introduction and Methodology

Public confidence in institutions evolves over time and is influenced by major national events and politics. The COVID-19 pandemic was the most recent event that altered everyday life, including social, economic, and political environments, and potentially changed Americans' trust in their government's institutions. This project investigates how Americans' confidence in major government programs and institutions (i.e., the military, media, Congress, the Supreme Court, and more) has changed from pre-pandemic (2012-2018) to during the pandemic period (2021-2022) and post-pandemic (2023-2024) \footnote{The federal COVID-19 PHE declaration ended on May 11, 2023.}. Using data from the General Social Survey (GSS), this study will examine whether these patterns differ across demographic groups such as race and sex.

Exploratory data analysis (EDA) revealed that the GSS has moved away from yearly surveys. Due to this I decided to include more years pre-pandemic to make up for the lack of data and the same was applied to the post-pandemic, turning it into during and post-pandemic years.
